SCI.ANIM.L07.01|What is a vertebrate?
how: Step 1. A backbone is a row of small bones down an animal’s back. An animal with a backbone is a vertebrate. Fish, frogs, snakes, birds and dogs all have one.

key: SCI.ANIM.L07.01|Most kinds of animals in the world have…
how: Step 3. Invertebrates win by far. Out of every 20 kinds of animals, about 19 have no backbone. Many, like insects and spiders, wear a hard shell outside instead.

SCI.ANIM.L07.02|Which clue tells you for sure that an animal is a bird?
how: Step 1. Vertebrates come in five groups: fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals. Each group has a clue of its own. Only birds have feathers. Only mammals have hair and feed their babies milk.

key: SCI.ANIM.L07.02|Which group has moist skin and starts life in the water, breathing with gills?
how: Step 2. Look at the skin. Fish have wet scales and fins. Amphibians, like frogs, have moist, smooth skin. Reptiles, like snakes and turtles, have dry scales.

how: Step 1. Scientists sort living things like a set of boxes, one inside another. Animals is a big box. Inside it is a smaller box, vertebrates. Inside that is mammals.

key: SCI.ANIM.L07.04|In which group are the members MOST alike?
how: Step 2. The smaller the box, the more alike the members. All animals are very different. Mammals share more. House cats share almost everything. One kind of living thing is called a species.

SCI.ANIM.L08.01|In a food chain, an arrow goes from the grass to the rabbit. What does that arrow show?
how: Step 1. In a food chain, each arrow shows where the energy goes. It goes FROM the one that is eaten TO the one that eats it.

key: SCI.ANIM.L08.01|Where does almost all the energy in a food chain first come from?
how: Step 2. Almost every food chain starts with the sun. Producers, like plants and algae, catch sunlight and store its energy in food. Everyone else eats.

key: SCI.ANIM.L08.01|In grass → grasshopper → frog → snake, which one is the secondary consumer?
how: Step 3. Name each level. The producer is first. The animal that eats it is the primary consumer. Whoever eats that one is the secondary consumer, then tertiary.

SCI.ANIM.L08.02|In a food web, three arrows point INTO the owl. What do those three arrows tell you?
how: Step 1. Read the arrows. Arrows pointing INTO an animal show what it eats. Arrows pointing OUT of it show who eats it.

key: SCI.ANIM.L08.02|How do you trace one food chain inside a big food web?
how: Step 2. To trace a chain, start at a producer and follow the arrows, one at a time, up to an animal that nothing eats. That road is one food chain.

key: SCI.ANIM.L08.02|A sparrow eats wheat seeds, and it also eats grasshoppers. What is the sparrow?
how: Step 3. One animal can sit on two levels. Eating seeds makes the sparrow a primary consumer. Eating grasshoppers, which eat plants, makes it a secondary consumer too.

SCI.ANIM.L08.03|A rabbit eats a lot of grass. Where does most of that energy go?
how: Step 1. Every living thing uses most of its food energy just to live: to move, grow, breathe and stay warm. That energy leaves its body as heat.

key: SCI.ANIM.L08.03|About how much of the energy at one level passes up to the next level?
how: Step 2. Only about 10 percent passes up to the next level: the part stored in the body that gets eaten. This is called the 10 percent rule.

key: SCI.ANIM.L08.03|Grass stores 10,000 units of energy. About how much reaches the rabbits that eat it?
how: Step 3. To find 10 percent, divide by 10: take one zero off the end. 10,000 → 1,000 → 100 → 10. Each step up keeps one tenth.

SCI.ANIM.L08.04|A plant takes in carbon dioxide from the air. Where did some of that carbon come from?
how: Step 2. Carbon goes round in a loop. Plants take carbon dioxide from the air to build food. Animals and decomposers use the food and breathe carbon dioxide back out.

key: SCI.ANIM.L08.04|Can energy go round and round in a loop, the way matter does?
how: Step 3. Energy does NOT loop. It comes in as sunlight, moves up the chain, and leaves as heat at every step. So every food web needs new sunlight every day.

SCI.PLANT.L08.01|Some living things are just one single cell. Which of these is only one cell?
how: Step 2. Some living things are just one cell: a bacterium, an amoeba, a yeast cell. Others are many-celled, like a tree or a fish. Their cells work together, and each kind has its own job.

key: SCI.PLANT.L08.01|Where do new cells come from?
how: Step 3. New cells come only from other cells. A cell grows, copies what is inside it, and splits into two new cells. Each of those can split again: 1, 2, 4, 8.

how: Step 2. Plant cells have three extras. Box: a stiff cell wall outside the membrane. Green: chloroplasts that make food from sunlight. Tank: one big vacuole full of water.

key: SCI.PLANT.L08.03|An animal cell has no stiff wall. What shape is it usually?
how: Step 3. Animal cells have a membrane, cytoplasm and a nucleus, but no cell wall and no chloroplasts. Without a wall, they are often round or uneven.

key: SCI.PLANT.L08.04|Which part is the gate that decides what goes in and out of the cell?
how: Step 3. The cell membrane is the gate. It lets food, water and air in and sends waste out. The cytoplasm is the jelly where the work happens. The vacuole stores water.

key: SCI.PLANT.L09.03|Which plant has WHITE flowers?
how: Step 2. A plant only shows the recessive trait when BOTH letters are small: pp is white. PP and Pp are both purple.

key: SCI.BODY.L09.04|What is the job of a scab?

key: SCI.BODY.L09.04|What should you do first with a small, clean scrape?
how: Step 3. Under the scab, NEW SKIN grows in from the edges. When it is ready, the scab falls off by itself, often in about 1 to 2 weeks. First wash the scrape with clean water and cover it.

how: A push moves something away from you. A pull moves something toward you.

key: SCI.PHYS.L01.02|You kick a ball. Is that a push or a pull?
how: A push or a pull can start something moving, stop it, or make it go a new way.

key: SCI.PHYS.L01.02|Which push makes the ball roll the farthest?

SCI.PHYS.L02.01|What makes a sound?
how: Every sound is made by something shaking back and forth very fast. This shaking is called vibration.

key: SCI.PHYS.L02.01|Hum and touch your throat. What do you feel?
how: Hit a drum and its top shakes. Pluck a string and it wiggles. Put your hand on your throat and hum. You can feel it buzz!

key: SCI.PHYS.L02.01|Which makes a louder sound?
how: A big shake makes a loud sound. A small shake makes a soft sound. When the shaking stops, the sound stops.

SCI.PHYS.L02.02|Why can't you see in a totally dark room?
how: We see things when light bounces off them and goes into our eyes. In a totally dark room, we cannot see anything.

key: SCI.PHYS.L02.02|Which one lets light pass right through?
how: Some things let light pass through, like a clear window. Some let a little light through, like wax paper. Some block the light, like a wooden door.

key: SCI.PHYS.L02.02|A flashlight shines on a ball. Where is the shadow?
how: When something blocks the light, it makes a shadow. The shadow is on the side away from the light.

how: Always measure with the same unit. Inches and centimeters are different sizes, so we never mix them in one measurement.

how: Everything is made of materials, like wood, metal, glass, cloth or plastic. Each material has properties: hard or soft, rough or smooth, bendy or stiff.

SCI.PHYS.L03.02|What happens to water in the freezer?
how: Cooling can change things too. Put water in the freezer and it freezes into ice.

key: SCI.PHYS.L03.02|Which change can be undone?
how: Some changes can be undone. Melted ice can freeze again. Some changes can never be undone. A cooked egg can never become raw again.

SCI.MATT.L04.01|What pulls a dropped ball to the ground?
how: Gravity is a pull that brings things down toward the earth. Drop a ball, and gravity pulls it to the ground.

key: SCI.MATT.L04.01|What keeps you from floating off into the sky?
how: Gravity holds you on the ground, keeps water in the oceans, and keeps the moon going around the earth.

SCI.MATT.L04.02|What does friction do to a sliding object?
how: Friction is a force that slows things down when two surfaces rub together.

key: SCI.MATT.L04.02|Which surface has the least friction?
how: Rough surfaces like carpet or sandpaper make lots of friction. Smooth surfaces like ice make little friction.

key: SCI.MATT.L04.02|Why do your hands get warm when you rub them?

SCI.MATT.L05.01|What is energy?
how: Energy is what makes things happen: move, light up, warm up or make sound.

key: SCI.MATT.L05.01|Which is a form of energy?
how: Energy comes in many forms: light, heat, motion, sound, electricity, and energy stored in food and fuel.

how: If there is a gap anywhere in the loop, electricity stops and the bulb goes out. A switch makes a gap on purpose.

key: SCI.MATT.L05.02|Which is a conductor?
how: Some materials let electricity through, like metals. They are conductors. Others block it, like plastic, rubber and wood. They are insulators.

key: SCI.MATT.L05.03|Which travels faster?

LIFE.FIN.L04.01|You get 3 answers right. Each one earns $1.00. How much do you earn?
how: In your lessons, every right answer earns $1.00. Finishing a whole lesson earns $10.00. Add them up to see what you earned.

key: LIFE.FIN.L04.01|Your balance says $25.50. How many whole dollars do you have?
how: Your balance shows at the top of the screen, like: Tashbar Bank balance $25.50. The number before the dot is dollars. The number after the dot is cents. So $25.50 is twenty-five dollars and fifty cents.

key: LIFE.FIN.L04.01|Before you can save or spend money, what must happen?
how: The skill underneath: Needs and Wants (Social Studies Level 2). Money pays for the things we need and the things we want. But first, money has to come in.

key: LIFE.FIN.L04.02|The price is $7. You pay $10. Hop 8, 9, 10. How many hops?
how: A new way: use a number line. Put your finger on the price. Hop by ones to the money you paid. Count the hops: that is your change.

key: LIFE.FIN.L04.02|A toy costs $3. How many $1 bills do you give?
how: A simpler step: pay with $1 bills only. Each $1 bill pays one dollar of the price.

key: LIFE.FIN.L04.02|Your balance is $10. You spend $4. Is your balance now bigger or smaller?
how: The skill underneath: Earning Money (Life and Money Level 4). You pay with money you earned. Spending makes your balance go down.

LIFE.BUD.L04.02|Which one is a saving goal?
how: A saving goal is something you save up for, like a new sefer or a ball. Pick the goal, find its price, and choose how much to save each week. Then count the weeks. Watching your savings grow is exciting!

key: LIFE.BUD.L04.02|Your goal is $6. You save $1 each week. How many weeks will it take?
how: A simpler step: save $1 each week. Then the number of weeks is the same as the number of dollars in the goal.

how: A schedule is a list of what happens in each part of the day, with the time. Reading your schedule tells you what comes next, so you are always ready. Planning which lessons you will do in each block makes you a strong learner!

key: LIFE.STUDY.L04.02|What should you do before a lesson starts?
how: Before you start learning, get ready. Have your things: a charged Chromebook, a pencil, paper. Do one task at a time. Keep only your lesson on the screen. A ready learner learns faster and finishes more!

key: LIFE.STUDY.L04.02|You are halfway through a math lesson. What is best?
how: One task at a time means you finish one thing before you start the next. Jumping between things makes both go slower.

key: LIFE.STUDY.L04.02|A friend wants to talk during your lesson. What can you say?
how: A distraction pulls your eyes and mind away from learning. If a friend talks to you during a lesson, you can kindly say: let's talk after my lesson.

how: A new way: think of a goalie. He is ready before the ball comes, and his eyes stay on the ball. A ready learner has his things before the lesson, and his eyes stay on the lesson.

key: LIFE.STUDY.L04.02|What should be on your screen during a lesson?
how: A simpler step: one rule. Only my lesson on the screen.

key: LIFE.STUDY.L04.02|Math lessons are next. What do you get ready?
how: The skill underneath: My Daily Plan (Life and Money Level 4). When you know what comes next, you can get the right things ready.

key: LIFE.FIN.L05.01|Which one is a need?
how: A smart shopper asks two questions before he buys. First: is it a need or a want? A need is something you must have, like food or a coat. A want is nice to have, like a toy. Needs come first. Second: which choice is the better deal? Smart shoppers make their money go further!

key: LIFE.FIN.L05.01|The same notebook costs $3 at one store and $5 at another. Which price is the better deal?
how: To compare prices, look at what you get for the money. If the item is the same, the lower price is the better deal.

key: LIFE.FIN.L05.01|A pack of 5 pens costs $10. How much is one pen?
how: A bigger pack can cost more but give more. Find the price of one. A pack of 4 pencils for $8 is $2 for each pencil.

LIFE.FIN.L05.01|When money is short, what should you buy first?

LIFE.FIN.L05.01|Bag A has 3 apples for $3. Bag B has 5 apples for $10. Which bag costs less for each apple?
LIFE.FIN.L05.01|On a smart shopping list, where do needs go?
how: A new way: the shopping list test. Write needs at the top of the list and wants at the bottom. Buy from the top down, and stop when the money runs out.

key: LIFE.FIN.L05.01|The same ball costs $9 or $7. Which price is cheaper?
how: A simpler step: one item, two prices. Pick the smaller number.

key: LIFE.FIN.L05.01|A cap costs $6. You pay $10. How much change do you get?
how: The skill underneath: Count and Pay (Life and Money Level 4). Before you shop, you must know how to pay and check your change.

key: LIFE.BUD.L05.01|You earn $50. You plan $20 for food and $15 for savings. How much is left for the other categories?
how: A budget must fit the money you have. If you earn $50, all the categories together can make $50, and no more.

key: LIFE.BUD.L05.01|Your food category has $20. You spent $13. How much is left for food?
how: Sticking to the budget means you never spend more than a category has. If food has $20 and you spent $14, you have $6 left for food.

how: A new way: a budget is like envelopes. Put the money for each category in its own envelope. When an envelope is empty, that category is done for the week.

key: LIFE.BUD.L05.01|You earn $10 and save $4. How much can you spend?
how: A simpler step: just two categories. Save some, and spend the rest.

key: LIFE.BUD.L05.01|Your goal is $20. You budget $5 for savings each week. How many weeks will it take?
how: The skill underneath: Saving Goal (Life and Money Level 4). Savings is one category in your budget, and it moves you toward your goal.

key: LIFE.FIN.L05.02|When you borrow money, what must you do?
how: Borrowing means using money that belongs to someone else, and you must pay it all back. Money you borrow is called a loan. Paying back on time keeps your word, and people will trust you. Borrowing is a big responsibility!

key: LIFE.FIN.L05.02|You borrow $20 from a store. The interest is $2. How much do you pay back?
how: Many banks and stores charge extra for a loan. The extra is called interest. Borrow $20 with $2 interest, and you pay back $22. The Torah says a Jew may not lend to, or borrow from, another Jew with interest. This is ribbis. The lender, the borrower, and even a guarantor or a witness all do an aveirah. A gemach lends with no extra. Ask your rebbe to learn more.

key: LIFE.FIN.L05.02|A $40 game is bought with a loan that adds $6 interest. What is the total cost?
how: Borrowing can cost more than saving up. A $30 bike with $5 interest costs $35 in all. Saving up first costs only $30.

how: A new way: borrowing money is like borrowing a library book. You must bring back the whole book, on time.

key: LIFE.FIN.L05.02|You borrow $7 with no interest. How much do you pay back?
how: A simpler step: no interest. You pay back exactly what you borrowed.

key: LIFE.FIN.L05.02|You earn $20 and must pay back $5 this week. How much is left for everything else?
how: The skill underneath: Weekly Budget (Life and Money Level 5). Paying back a loan is one category in your budget.

key: LIFE.FIN.L05.03|Yossi keeps $50 at home and $50 in the bank. The $50 at home gets lost. How much does he still have?
how: A bank keeps money safe and keeps a record of it. If you lose your wallet, the money in the bank is still yours.

key: LIFE.FIN.L05.03|Which coat is most likely to come back if it is lost?
how: Write your name on your things. A lost coat with a name tag can find its way back to you.

how: A new way: think like a guard. A guard asks: what could go wrong, and how do I stop it?

key: LIFE.FIN.L05.03|Where should your money stay when you are out?
how: A simpler step: one rule. Money stays closed up: in a wallet, a pocket or the bank.

key: LIFE.FIN.L05.03|You bought a new ball. How do you keep it from getting lost?
how: The skill underneath: Smart Shopper (Life and Money Level 5). You chose carefully what to buy. Keep it safe so your money is not wasted.

key: LIFE.STUDY.L05.01|Which helps you remember more?
how: Reading something again and again feels easy, but it is not the best way to remember. The best way is to quiz yourself: cover the answer and try to remember it. Then practice again a few days later. Your memory gets stronger every time it has to work!

key: LIFE.STUDY.L05.01|Shmuel must learn 10 new words. What is the best way?
LIFE.STUDY.L05.01|Which one is quizzing yourself?
LIFE.STUDY.L05.01|Dovid is learning a mishnah by heart. What helps him most?
LIFE.STUDY.L05.01|Which way builds a stronger memory?
LIFE.STUDY.L05.01|What should be on your screen while you quiz yourself?
how: The skill underneath: Ready to Learn (Life and Money Level 4). A self-quiz works best with your things ready and no distractions.

key: LIFE.STUDY.L05.02|When should you check your work?
how: Before you hand in your work, check it. Read the question again: does your answer match what it asked? For math, check with the opposite. Checking catches mistakes before anyone else sees them!

key: LIFE.STUDY.L05.02|Moshe wrote 36 + 18 = 54. Check: 54 − 18 = 36. Is his answer right?
how: To check adding, subtract. 27 + 15 = 42. Check: 42 − 15 = 27. It matches, so the answer is right.

key: LIFE.STUDY.L05.02|The question asks how many cookies are left. Mendy wrote the total. What should he do?
how: Read the question again to see what it asks. If it asks how many are left, your answer must be how many are left, not the total.

how: A simpler step: just reread. Read the question once more and make sure your answer fits it.

key: LIFE.BUD.L06.01|Look at the ledger. What is the balance after the boss test?
how: Money in is added. Money out is subtracted. Start with $40 and earn $10: $50. Spend $6: $44.
pic:

key: LIFE.BUD.L06.01|Your balance is $52. You earn $10. What is the new balance?
LIFE.BUD.L06.01|Your balance is $35. You spend $8. What is the new balance?
LIFE.BUD.L06.01|You start with $20. You earn $15, then spend $12. What is the balance now?
LIFE.BUD.L06.01|Your balance is $48. You spend $9. What is the new balance?
LIFE.BUD.L06.01|You start with $60. You spend $25, then earn $10. What is the balance now?
LIFE.BUD.L06.01|On a money scoreboard, what does earning do to the score?
how: A new way: a ledger is like a scoreboard for your money. Every play changes the score, and the scoreboard always shows the latest score.

key: LIFE.BUD.L06.01|Which one shows what really happened to your money?
how: The skill underneath: Weekly Budget (Life and Money Level 5). A budget is the plan. A ledger shows what really happened.

key: LIFE.FIN.L06.01|What is 10% of $50?
LIFE.FIN.L06.01|What is 10% of $80?
LIFE.FIN.L06.01|Why does the snowball grow faster as it rolls?
how: A new way: compound interest is like a snowball rolling downhill. It picks up snow, and the bigger it gets, the more snow it picks up.

key: LIFE.FIN.L06.01|What is one tenth of $30?
how: A simpler step: 10% is one tenth. Split the amount into 10 equal parts and take one.

key: LIFE.FIN.L06.02|Which words are pressure words?
how: Pressure words try to rush you: ONLY TODAY, HURRY, LAST CHANCE. When you feel rushed, slow down.

key: LIFE.FIN.L06.02|You see a game you suddenly want. What does the wait-a-day rule say?
how: The wait-a-day rule: if you want something that is not a need, wait a day before you buy. If you still want it tomorrow and it fits your budget, then decide.

key: LIFE.FIN.L06.02|An ad says: Every kid has one! Which trick is that?
LIFE.FIN.L06.02|An ad says the toy is the BEST in the world. What should you think?
LIFE.FIN.L06.02|A sign says SALE: $20, was $30. How much do you save?
LIFE.FIN.L06.02|The sale saves $10, but the toy was not on your list. What is the smart choice?
LIFE.FIN.L06.02|A website shows a timer: 5 minutes left to buy! What is the timer for?
LIFE.FIN.L06.02|Abba sees a car ad that says LAST CHANCE, LOW PRICE. What should he do?
LIFE.FIN.L06.02|Which one is a pressure trick?
LIFE.FIN.L06.02|A $15 hat is on sale for $9. How much do you save?
LIFE.FIN.L06.02|After waiting a day, you still want something, and it fits your budget. What now?
LIFE.FIN.L06.02|An ad shows a famous player wearing the shoes. What does it want you to think?
how: A new way: be an ad detective. For each ad, ask: what trick is it using, and what does it want me to do?

key: LIFE.FIN.L06.02|You did not want a toy until you saw an ad for it. Is it a need?
how: A simpler step: one question. Do I need it, or does the ad just make me want it?

key: LIFE.FIN.L06.02|When you go shopping, what comes first?
how: The skill underneath: Smart Shopper (Life and Money Level 5). Needs come first, and you compare before you buy.

key: LIFE.STUDY.L06.01|Which is a good short note for: The Nile River is the longest river in Africa?
how: Use short forms: arrows, numbers and signs. Water turns into ice at 32 degrees can become: water → ice at 32°.

key: LIFE.STUDY.L06.01|Which note is short and clear?
LIFE.STUDY.L06.01|What does an arrow → often mean in notes?
LIFE.STUDY.L06.01|Your note says: light → day 1. Which question can you quiz yourself with?
LIFE.STUDY.L06.01|Put the note-taking steps in order.
LIFE.STUDY.L06.01|Abba is on a long phone call about a simcha. What helps him remember the date and place?
LIFE.STUDY.L06.01|Which is a good short note for: George Washington was the first President of the United States?
LIFE.STUDY.L06.01|The rebbe says: Volcanoes are mountains that erupt with lava. What is the key word?
how: A simpler step: one key word. Write just the most important word you hear.

key: LIFE.STUDY.L06.02|Put the science fair steps in order.
LIFE.STUDY.L06.02|Which one is a good small step?
LIFE.STUDY.L06.02|Abba is making a bar mitzvah in 8 weeks. What helps him most?
LIFE.STUDY.L06.02|A project is due in 20 days and has 4 steps. How many days can each step take?
LIFE.STUDY.L06.02|When you bake a cake, what comes first?
how: A simpler step: just two steps. What comes first, and what comes next?

key: LIFE.STUDY.L06.02|Which project step uses your notes the most?
how: The skill underneath: Notes That Work (Life and Money Level 6). Your research notes are one step of the project.

key: LIFE.STUDY.L06.03|Which one is a goal?
how: A goal is something you aim for, like mastering 8 skills this week. A habit is something you do every day without thinking, like learning right after breakfast. Good habits help you reach your goals!

key: LIFE.STUDY.L06.03|Which goal is clearer?
how: A clear goal has a number and a time: master 8 skills by Friday. Not: learn more.

key: LIFE.STUDY.L06.03|Your goal is 12 skills in 4 days. How many skills a day?
how: Track your goal every day. 8 skills in 4 days means 2 skills a day: 8 ÷ 4 = 2.

key: LIFE.STUDY.L06.03|Your goal is 10 skills this week. You have mastered 6. How many more do you need?
LIFE.STUDY.L06.03|Which one is a good habit for learning?
LIFE.STUDY.L06.03|Your goal is 15 skills in 5 days. How many skills a day?
LIFE.STUDY.L06.03|You met your goal 3 weeks in a row. What should you do next?
LIFE.STUDY.L06.03|You missed your goal this week. What is the best next step?
LIFE.STUDY.L06.03|Yossi wants to finish a whole sefer of Mishnayos. Which plan helps most?
LIFE.STUDY.L06.03|Your goal is 8 skills. You have mastered 5. How many more do you need?
LIFE.STUDY.L06.03|What makes a goal clear?
LIFE.STUDY.L06.03|Your goal is 20 skills in 4 days. How many skills a day?
LIFE.STUDY.L06.03|What makes a habit easier?
how: A new way: a habit is like a path across the grass. The more you walk it, the clearer and easier it gets.

key: LIFE.STUDY.L06.03|Which one is a good goal for today?
how: A simpler step: just one small goal for today.

key: LIFE.STUDY.L06.03|Your weekly goal is 10 skills over 5 days. What is one daily step?
how: The skill underneath: Big Project Planner (Life and Money Level 6). A weekly goal is like a project: break it into daily steps.

key: LIFE.FIN.L07.01|An electrician earns $40 an hour. How much does he earn in 8 hours?
how: Pay = hourly rate × hours. A helper earns $15 an hour and an electrician earns $40 an hour. In 8 hours, that is $120 versus $320.

key: LIFE.FIN.L07.01|A plumber earns $35 an hour and a helper earns $15 an hour. How much more does the plumber earn each hour?
LIFE.FIN.L07.01|Which job usually needs the most training?
LIFE.FIN.L07.01|Yossi earns $12 an hour. After a course, he earns $18 an hour. How much more does he earn in 10 hours?
LIFE.FIN.L07.01|What is a trade?
LIFE.FIN.L07.01|Training raises pay by $4 an hour. How much more is that in a 40-hour week?
LIFE.FIN.L07.01|What usually raises how much a person can earn?
LIFE.FIN.L07.01|You earn $10 an hour. How much do you earn in 3 hours?
how: A simpler step: pay for one hour, then count up. $10 an hour for 3 hours: $10, $20, $30.

key: LIFE.FIN.L07.02|Gross pay is $600. Taxes are $120. What is the take-home pay?
how: Take-home = gross − taxes. Gross $500, taxes $100: take-home $400.

key: LIFE.FIN.L07.02|Gross pay is $400. Taxes are 20%. How much is taken out for taxes?
how: Taxes are often a percent of gross pay. 20% means 20 out of every 100. On $500, 20% is $100.

key: LIFE.FIN.L07.02|Gross pay is $800. Taxes are $150. What is the take-home pay?
LIFE.FIN.L07.02|Gross pay is $300. Taxes are 10%. How much is taken out?
LIFE.FIN.L07.02|Gross pay is $1,000. Taxes are 20%. What is the take-home pay?
LIFE.FIN.L07.02|Which is bigger: gross pay or take-home pay?
LIFE.FIN.L07.02|What do taxes pay for?
LIFE.FIN.L07.02|Chaim's brother works 20 hours at $15 an hour. $60 is taken out for taxes. What is his take-home pay?
LIFE.FIN.L07.02|Gross pay is $700. Taxes are $140. What is the take-home pay?
LIFE.FIN.L07.02|Gross pay is $500. Taxes are 10%. What is the take-home pay?
LIFE.FIN.L07.02|What is gross pay?
LIFE.FIN.L07.02|Gross is $100 and taxes are $20. What is left?
how: A simpler step: just subtract. Gross minus taxes.

key: LIFE.FIN.L07.02|You earn $20 an hour for 5 hours. What is your gross pay?
how: The skill underneath: Jobs and Skills (Life and Money Level 7). Gross pay is rate × hours.

key: LIFE.BUD.L07.01|Which one is a fixed cost?
how: A household budget plans a whole month. Fixed costs are the same every month, like rent and tuition. Changing costs go up and down, like food and electricity. Plan the fixed costs first, because they must be paid!

key: LIFE.BUD.L07.01|Take-home pay is $4,000. Fixed costs are $2,500. How much is left for everything else?
how: Take-home pay minus fixed costs = money left for changing costs and savings. $3,000 − $1,800 fixed = $1,200.

key: LIFE.BUD.L07.01|Food cost $300, $400 and $500 in the last three months. What is the average?
how: Changing costs need an estimate. Use the average of the last few months: add them and divide by how many. $500, $600 and $400 average to $500.

key: LIFE.BUD.L07.01|Which one is a changing cost?
LIFE.BUD.L07.01|Take-home pay is $3,500. Fixed costs are $2,000. How much is left?
LIFE.BUD.L07.01|Rent is $1,500, tuition is $800 and insurance is $200. What are the total fixed costs?
LIFE.BUD.L07.01|Electricity cost $100, $150 and $200. What is the average?
LIFE.BUD.L07.01|The month's costs add up to more than take-home pay. What should the family do?
LIFE.BUD.L07.01|A shul's monthly budget: $6,000 comes in. Rent is $2,000 and the rav's salary is $3,000. How much is left for other costs?
LIFE.BUD.L07.01|Which cost is the same every month?
LIFE.BUD.L07.01|Take-home pay is $5,000. Fixed costs are $3,200. How much is left?
LIFE.BUD.L07.01|Phone bills were $40, $50 and $60. What is the average?
LIFE.BUD.L07.01|You take home $1,000. Fixed costs are $600. What is left?
how: A simpler step: just two numbers. Money in minus fixed costs.

key: LIFE.BUD.L07.01|A monthly budget starts from which number?
how: The skill underneath: Paycheck Math (Life and Money Level 7). A budget starts from take-home pay, not gross pay.

key: LIFE.FIN.L07.03|You owe $500. The card charges 2% a month. If you pay nothing, how much do you owe next month?
how: Unpaid debt grows. Owe $1,000 at 2% a month and pay nothing: 2% of $1,000 is $20, so next month you owe $1,020.

key: LIFE.FIN.L07.03|You owe $200. The card charges 2% a month. How much interest is added this month?
LIFE.FIN.L07.03|You owe $1,000 and pay $100. How much do you still owe, before interest?
LIFE.FIN.L07.03|Which one is the better habit?
LIFE.FIN.L07.03|You owe $300 at 2% a month and pay nothing. How much do you owe next month?
LIFE.FIN.L07.03|Someone owes a bank $2,000 on a credit card at 2% a month. How much interest is added in one month?
LIFE.FIN.L07.03|You owe $400. The card charges 2% a month. If you pay nothing, how much do you owe next month?
LIFE.FIN.L07.03|What makes the debt hole deeper each month?
how: A new way: debt is like a hole that keeps getting deeper. Interest digs more every month. Paying only a little is like scooping out one spoonful while the hole grows.

key: LIFE.FIN.L07.03|What is 2% of $100?
how: A simpler step: 1% is one hundredth. So 2% of $100 is $2.

key: LIFE.FIN.L07.03|On a loan, who does the interest help?
how: The skill underneath: Interest Grows (Life and Money Level 6). On savings, interest helps you. On debt, the same math works against you.

key: LIFE.FIN.L07.04|Which detail should you never share with a stranger online?
LIFE.FIN.L07.04|A caller says: Pay now or your account closes in 10 minutes! Which trick is that?
LIFE.FIN.L07.04|A scammer took $40 from each of three families. How much did he take in all?
LIFE.FIN.L07.04|An email has a strange link and spelling mistakes. What should you do?
LIFE.FIN.L07.04|Abba gets a call: Your credit card is locked; tell me the code on the back. What should he do?
LIFE.FIN.L07.04|Which payment request is a big warning sign?
LIFE.FIN.L07.04|Does a real bank ask for your password by email?
LIFE.FIN.L07.04|In the fishing idea, what is the prize message?
how: A new way: a scammer is like a fisherman with bait. The prize or the scary message is the bait. Do not bite!

key: LIFE.FIN.L07.04|Keeping your password secret is like what?
how: The skill underneath: Keeping Things Safe (Life and Money Level 5). Protecting your details is like locking your door.

key: LIFE.STUDY.L07.01|On a practice test you got 18 of 20 right. How many did you miss?
how: After a practice test, find what you missed and study those first.

key: LIFE.STUDY.L07.01|You got 15 of 20 right on a practice test. How many did you miss?
LIFE.STUDY.L07.01|After a practice test, what should you study first?
LIFE.STUDY.L07.01|Put the test-prep steps in order.
LIFE.STUDY.L07.01|A boy getting ready to lein his bar mitzvah parsha has 6 weeks. What is the best plan?
LIFE.STUDY.L07.01|Why take a practice test?
LIFE.STUDY.L07.01|You got 22 of 25 right. How many did you miss?
LIFE.STUDY.L07.01|In the race idea, what is a practice race like?
how: A new way: test prep is like training for a race. A runner trains a little every day and runs practice races. He does not run his first mile on race day.

key: LIFE.STUDY.L07.01|Which one is a good plan for today?
how: A simpler step: one day, one topic. Study just one topic today and quiz yourself on it.

key: LIFE.STUDY.L07.01|Your goal is 6 topics in 3 days. What is the daily step?
how: The skill underneath: Goals and Habits (Life and Money Level 6). A study plan is a goal split into daily steps.

key: LIFE.FIN.L08.01|What does risk mean in investing?
how: Investing means using money to buy something that may grow in value, like a share of a company (stock). Investments can earn more than a savings account, but they carry risk: the value can also go down. Higher possible reward usually comes with higher risk. (Some investments raise halachic questions. Ask your rebbe.)

key: LIFE.FIN.L08.01|Which choice has the most risk?
LIFE.FIN.L08.01|You split $500 equally among 5 companies. How much goes into each?
LIFE.FIN.L08.01|A farmer plants wheat, corn and beans instead of only wheat. Why?
LIFE.FIN.L08.01|You split $400 equally among 4 companies. One fails completely. How much do you lose?
LIFE.FIN.L08.01|Higher possible reward usually comes with what?
LIFE.FIN.L08.01|Why carry eggs in many baskets?
how: A new way: do not put all your eggs in one basket. If that one basket drops, every egg breaks.

key: LIFE.FIN.L08.01|Which one is safer and steadier?
how: The skill underneath: Interest Grows (Life and Money Level 6). Savings interest is safe and steady. Investing can grow more, but it can also lose.

key: LIFE.FIN.L08.02|Car damage costs $2,000. The deductible is $500. How much does insurance pay?
how: A deductible is the part you pay yourself before insurance pays. Damage $3,000, deductible $500: you pay $500 and insurance pays $2,500.

key: LIFE.FIN.L08.02|Which kind of insurance helps pay doctor and hospital bills?
LIFE.FIN.L08.02|200 families each pay $50 into a pool. How much is in the pool?
LIFE.FIN.L08.02|In a simcha gemach, 100 families each give $10 a month. How much does it collect in a month?
LIFE.FIN.L08.02|Which kind of insurance pays if your house has a fire?
LIFE.FIN.L08.02|In the snack fund idea, who pays in?
how: A new way: insurance is like a class snack fund. Everyone puts in $1, and whoever forgets his lunch gets a sandwich from the fund.

key: LIFE.FIN.L08.02|A caller offers super-cheap insurance if you pay today in gift cards. What is it?
how: The skill underneath: Scams and Fraud (Life and Money Level 7). Fake insurance offers are a common scam. Check with a parent before buying.

key: LIFE.BUD.L08.01|Which way usually costs less in total?
how: For a big purchase, like a car or a computer, you can save up first or borrow and pay over time. Borrowing gets it sooner but usually costs more because of interest. Always compare the total cost before you decide! (Between Jews, the halachos of ribbis apply. Ask your rebbe.)

key: LIFE.BUD.L08.01|A computer costs $900 cash, or $100 a month for 10 months. What is the total if you pay monthly?
how: Total cost of paying monthly = monthly payment × number of months. $100 a month for 12 months is $1,200.

key: LIFE.BUD.L08.01|A phone costs $500 cash, or $50 a month for 12 months. What is the total if you pay monthly?
LIFE.BUD.L08.01|The cash price is $500. The monthly payments add up to $600. How much extra do the payments cost?
LIFE.BUD.L08.01|You want a $400 item. You save $50 a month. How many months until you can pay cash?
LIFE.BUD.L08.01|Which question should you ask before a big purchase?
LIFE.BUD.L08.01|A couch costs $1,200 cash, or $110 a month for 12 months. Which way costs less?
LIFE.BUD.L08.01|A family needs a $20,000 car. Borrowing adds $3,000 in interest. What is the total cost if they borrow?
LIFE.BUD.L08.01|A laptop costs $800 cash, or $75 a month for 12 months. What is the total if you pay monthly?
LIFE.BUD.L08.01|The cash price is $300. The monthly payments add up to $360. How much extra is borrowing?
LIFE.BUD.L08.01|You want a $600 item and save $100 a month. How many months until you can pay cash?
LIFE.BUD.L08.01|In the line idea, what is the skip-the-line ticket?
how: A new way: borrowing is like buying a ticket to skip the line. You get the item sooner, but the ticket costs extra.

key: LIFE.BUD.L08.01|$20 a month for 5 months is how much?
how: A simpler step: payment × months.

key: LIFE.BUD.L08.01|What makes borrowing cost more than paying cash?
how: The skill underneath: Credit Cards and Loans (Life and Money Level 7). Interest is what makes borrowing cost more.

key: LIFE.FIN.L08.03|What is profit?
how: A small business sells something people want. Start-up costs are what you spend to begin, like tools and supplies. Revenue is all the money from sales. Profit is what is left after costs: revenue − costs. A good business owner tracks every number!

key: LIFE.FIN.L08.03|You sell 40 challah covers at $15 each. What is the revenue?
how: Revenue = price × number sold. Sell 30 cups of lemonade at $2: revenue $60.

key: LIFE.FIN.L08.03|Revenue is $600 and costs are $250. What is the profit?
how: Profit = revenue − costs. Revenue $60, costs $25: profit $35.

key: LIFE.FIN.L08.03|You sell 25 bookmarks at $2 each. What is the revenue?
LIFE.FIN.L08.03|Revenue is $120 and costs are $45. What is the profit?
LIFE.FIN.L08.03|Which one is a start-up cost for a car wash business?
LIFE.FIN.L08.03|Each item costs you $3 to make. You sell it for $5. What is the profit on one item?
LIFE.FIN.L08.03|Each item costs $4 to make and sells for $7. You sell 20. What is the total profit?
LIFE.FIN.L08.03|The school workshop builds birdhouses. Wood costs $6 each and they sell for $15. They sell 10. What is the profit?
LIFE.FIN.L08.03|You sell 50 cookies at $3 each. What is the revenue?
LIFE.FIN.L08.03|Revenue is $900 and costs are $400. What is the profit?
LIFE.FIN.L08.03|Each item costs $2 to make and sells for $6. You sell 30. What is the total profit?
LIFE.FIN.L08.03|You collect $50 and pay $20 for supplies. What is left in the cash box?
how: A new way: profit is what is left in the cash box after you pay for everything you used.

key: LIFE.FIN.L08.03|An item costs $1 to make and sells for $4. What is the profit on one?
how: A simpler step: profit on one item = selling price − cost to make it.

key: LIFE.STUDY.L08.01|Which task should come first?
how: Managing time means deciding what to do and when. Put first things first: important tasks with close due dates come before fun extras. Plan the whole week, block by block. A good plan leaves time for everything that matters!

key: LIFE.STUDY.L08.01|Which one is important and due soon?
how: Sort tasks by two questions: Is it important? Is it due soon? Important and due soon goes first.

key: LIFE.STUDY.L08.01|Which task can wait?
LIFE.STUDY.L08.01|Your tasks take 15, 25 and 20 minutes. How many minutes in all?
LIFE.STUDY.L08.01|You have 5 tasks to finish over 5 days. What is a good plan?
LIFE.STUDY.L08.01|Put these in first-things-first order.
LIFE.STUDY.L08.01|Before Pesach, Abba has a lot to do. What helps him most?
LIFE.STUDY.L08.01|Which task comes first?
LIFE.STUDY.L08.01|You have 90 minutes. Your tasks take 30 and 45 minutes. How many minutes are left?
LIFE.STUDY.L08.01|What does first things first mean?
LIFE.STUDY.L08.01|In the jar idea, what are the big rocks?
how: A new way: big rocks first. If you fill a jar with sand first, the big rocks do not fit. Put the big rocks in first, and the sand fills in around them.

key: LIFE.STUDY.L08.01|A quiz tomorrow or a project next week: which is due sooner?
how: A simpler step: one question. What is due soonest?

key: LIFE.STUDY.L08.01|Your test is in 4 days and has 8 topics. How many topics a day?
how: The skill underneath: Test Prep (Life and Money Level 7). Planning your study days is time management.

key: LIFE.STUDY.L08.02|What is the first step in reading a textbook chapter?
how: Reading a textbook is different from reading a story. First preview: look at the title, headings, pictures and bold words. Then ask questions you want answered, and read to find the answers. At the end, summarize in your own words. This turns reading into real learning!

key: LIFE.STUDY.L08.02|The heading is: Causes of the Civil War. Which question does it become?
how: Turn each heading into a question. The heading How Volcanoes Form becomes: How do volcanoes form?

key: LIFE.STUDY.L08.02|Which one is a summary?
how: A summary is short: the main ideas in your own words, not every detail.

key: LIFE.STUDY.L08.02|Which parts do you look at in a preview?
LIFE.STUDY.L08.02|The heading is: How Plants Make Food. Which question does it become?
LIFE.STUDY.L08.02|Why do bold words matter in a textbook?
LIFE.STUDY.L08.02|A chapter has 4 headings. You make one question for each heading. How many questions do you make?
LIFE.STUDY.L08.02|Put the read-to-learn steps in order.
LIFE.STUDY.L08.02|Abba reads the instructions before building a new sukkah. What should he do first?
LIFE.STUDY.L08.02|What should a summary have?
LIFE.STUDY.L08.02|The heading is: The Water Cycle. Which question does it become?
LIFE.STUDY.L08.02|Why turn headings into questions?
LIFE.STUDY.L08.02|The heading is: Why Bees Matter. Which one is the question?
how: A simpler step: just one heading. Add who, what, why or how to make it a question.

key: LIFE.STUDY.L08.02|Where can your chapter summary go?
how: The skill underneath: Notes That Work (Life and Money Level 6). Your summary can become your notes.

key: LIFE.FIN.L09.01|What does a higher credit score show?
how: A credit score is a number that shows lenders how well you handle borrowed money. It usually runs from about 300 to 850, and higher is better. A good score makes it easier and cheaper to rent an apartment or get a loan later. You build it one on-time payment at a time!

key: LIFE.FIN.L09.01|Which one builds a good credit score?
how: What builds a score: paying every bill on time, and using only a small part of your credit limit. What damages it: late or missed payments, and maxing out cards.

key: LIFE.FIN.L09.01|You owe $200 on a card with a $1,000 limit. What percent of your limit are you using?
how: Credit use = what you owe ÷ your limit. Owe $300 on a $1,000 limit: 300 ÷ 1,000 = 30%. Lower is better; many experts suggest staying under 30%.

key: LIFE.FIN.L09.01|Which one damages a credit score?
LIFE.FIN.L09.01|You owe $500 on a $1,000 limit. What percent are you using?
LIFE.FIN.L09.01|One person uses 10% of his limit and another uses 90%. Whose score is likely better?
LIFE.FIN.L09.01|Why does a credit score matter?
LIFE.FIN.L09.01|You owe $150 on a $500 limit. What percent are you using?
LIFE.FIN.L09.01|Two families want to rent the same apartment, and the landlord checks credit. Which family does he likely choose?
LIFE.FIN.L09.01|You owe $400 on a $2,000 limit. What percent are you using?
LIFE.FIN.L09.01|Which habit builds credit?
LIFE.FIN.L09.01|Is a higher or a lower credit score better?
LIFE.FIN.L09.01|In this idea, what is an on-time payment?
how: A new way: a credit score is like a reputation. Every time you keep your word, people trust you more. Break it, and trust drops.

key: LIFE.FIN.L09.01|You owe $100 on a $1,000 limit. What percent are you using?
how: A simpler step: owe $100 on a $1,000 limit. 100 is one tenth of 1,000, and one tenth is 10%.

key: LIFE.FIN.L09.02|Where does the money for a debit card purchase come from?
how: A checking account holds money for everyday spending. A debit card takes money straight from it. Unlike a credit card, a debit card spends your own money, so you cannot spend more than you have without being declined or paying fees. Keep track so you never overdraw!

key: LIFE.FIN.L09.02|Your checking account has $600. You spend $75 and $150 with your debit card. What is the balance?
how: Balance after purchases: start with $500, spend $45 and $120, and $335 is left.

LIFE.FIN.L09.02|How is a debit card different from a credit card?
LIFE.FIN.L09.02|Your account has $900. You spend $250 and $100. What is the balance?
LIFE.FIN.L09.02|What should you never share with anyone?
LIFE.FIN.L09.02|When you use a debit card, whose money do you spend?
how: A new way: a checking account is like your wallet kept at the bank. A debit card is like reaching into it.

key: LIFE.FIN.L09.02|You start with $100 and spend $30. What is the balance?
how: A simpler step: balance = start − spending.

key: LIFE.BUD.L09.01|Yom Tov costs for the year are $2,400. How much should the family save each month?
how: Monthly saving for a yearly cost = yearly cost ÷ 12. If Pesach costs $1,200, save $100 a month.

key: LIFE.BUD.L09.01|A family earns $50,000 a year. What is one tenth, for maaser?
how: Tzedakah for the year: many families give one tenth of income, maaser, as in Level 4. Income $60,000: maaser $6,000. Ask your rebbe how your family does it.

LIFE.BUD.L09.01|Tuition extras cost $1,800 a year. How much should be saved each month?
LIFE.BUD.L09.01|A family earns $40,000. What is one tenth?
LIFE.BUD.L09.01|What happens if you do not plan for once-a-year costs?
LIFE.BUD.L09.01|A cost of $120 a year is how much a month?
how: A simpler step: yearly cost ÷ 12 months.

key: LIFE.BUD.L09.01|Which way is cheaper for a big cost?
how: The skill underneath: Big Purchase Plan (Life and Money Level 8). Saving ahead for a big cost is cheaper than borrowing.

key: LIFE.FIN.L09.03|A course costs $6,000 and raises pay by $3,000 a year. How many years to earn back the cost?
how: Training costs money now but raises income later. A $5,000 course that adds $5,000 a year in pay earns back its cost in 1 year.

key: LIFE.FIN.L09.03|A trade course costs $8,000 and raises pay by $4,000 a year. How many years to earn back the cost?
LIFE.FIN.L09.03|You save $200 a month for 5 years. How much do you put in, before growth?
LIFE.FIN.L09.03|You save $75 a month for 4 years. How much do you put in, before growth?
LIFE.FIN.L09.03|A course costs $10,000 and raises pay by $5,000 a year. How many years to earn back the cost?
LIFE.FIN.L09.03|How many months are in 5 years?
how: A simpler step: months = years × 12.

key: LIFE.FIN.L09.03|Why spread long-term savings across many investments?
how: The skill underneath: Investing Basics (Life and Money Level 8). Long-term savings can be spread out so they grow and stay safer.

key: LIFE.STUDY.L09.01|What is the first step in teaching yourself something new?
how: You can teach yourself almost anything with a plan. Pick one skill. Break it into small parts. Find good sources, like a book, a rebbe or an expert. Practice a little every day, and check your progress each week. This is the skill behind every other skill!

key: LIFE.STUDY.L09.01|A skill has 12 parts. You learn 3 parts a week. How many weeks will it take?
how: Break the skill into parts and plan the weeks. 10 parts at 2 a week takes 5 weeks.

key: LIFE.STUDY.L09.01|You try without help and get stuck on one step. What should you practice next?
how: Check your progress: try the skill without help. Whatever you cannot do yet is what you practice next.

key: LIFE.STUDY.L09.01|Which one is a good source for learning a new skill?

LIFE.STUDY.L09.01|Avi wants to learn to fix bikes. Which plan is best?
LIFE.STUDY.L09.01|A skill has 15 parts. You learn 5 a week. How many weeks will it take?
LIFE.STUDY.L09.01|Why check your progress each week?
LIFE.STUDY.L09.01|Which goal is clearer for learning a new skill?
LIFE.STUDY.L09.01|In the ladder idea, what is one rung?
how: A new way: learning a skill is like climbing a ladder. Each rung is one small part. You cannot jump to the top.

key: LIFE.STUDY.L09.01|Which one is a good learning plan for today?
how: A simpler step: today, just one small part.

key: LIFE.STUDY.L09.01|What helps you learn from a how-to book?
how: The skill underneath: Manage Your Time and Read to Learn (Life and Money Level 8). Plan your practice time and read your sources well.

key: LIFE.BUD.L09.02|Look at the card. What is your hourly pay?
how: Time to put it all together! In this simulated year you have a job, pay taxes, give tzedakah, pay your bills and save. Read the card carefully: every number matters. Let's see if your first year out works!

key: LIFE.BUD.L09.02|Look at the card. What is your gross pay for one week?
how: Weekly gross = rate × hours. To keep it simple, the card counts one month as 4 weeks.

key: LIFE.BUD.L09.02|Look at the card. Your monthly gross is $3,200. What are the taxes for the month?
how: Monthly gross = weekly × 4 = $3,200. Then 20% comes out for taxes, and the rest is take-home pay.
